<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Synthetic\Accessors\Formats;

use Synthetic\Accessors\Accessor;

/** Reads `KEY=value` lines. Blank lines and lines that start with `#` are skipped; a value may be wrapped in one pair of matching quotes. */
final class EnvAccessor implements Accessor
{
    /** @var array<string, string> */
    private array $values = [];

    public function __construct(string $source)
    {
        foreach (preg_split('/\r?\n/', $source) ?: [] as $raw) {
            $line = trim($raw);
            if ($line === '' || str_starts_with($line, '#')) {
                continue;
            }
            $eq = strpos($line, '=');
            if ($eq === false || $eq === 0) {
                continue;
            }
            $key = trim(substr($line, 0, $eq));
            $value = trim(substr($line, $eq + 1));
            if (strlen($value) >= 2 && ($value[0] === '"' || $value[0] === "'") && $value[strlen($value) - 1] === $value[0]) {
                $value = substr($value, 1, -1);
            }
            $this->values[$key] = $value;
        }
    }

    public function get(string $key, ?string $fallback = null): ?string
    {
        return $this->values[$key] ?? $fallback;
    }

    public function has(string $key): bool
    {
        return array_key_exists($key, $this->values);
    }

    public function all(): array
    {
        return $this->values;
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

require __DIR__ . '/../src/Accessor.php';
require __DIR__ . '/../src/Formats/EnvAccessor.php';
require __DIR__ . '/../src/Formats/JsonAccessor.php';

use Synthetic\Accessors\Formats\EnvAccessor;
use Synthetic\Accessors\Formats\JsonAccessor;

$failures = 0;
function check(string $name, bool $ok): void
{
    global $failures;
    echo ($ok ? "ok   " : "FAIL ") . $name . "\n";
    if (!$ok) {
        $failures++;
    }
}

$env = new EnvAccessor("HOST=localhost\nPORT=3000\n");
check('reads KEY=value lines', $env->get('HOST') === 'localhost' && $env->get('PORT') === '3000');

$env = new EnvAccessor("# a comment\n\nKEY=value\n");
check('skips blank lines and comments', $env->all() === ['KEY' => 'value']);

$env = new EnvAccessor("A=\"one two\"\nB='three'\n");
check('strips one pair of matching quotes', $env->get('A') === 'one two' && $env->get('B') === 'three');

$env = new EnvAccessor('KEY=value');
check('answers the fallback for a key that is not there', $env->get('MISSING', 'none') === 'none' && $env->has('KEY') && !$env->has('MISSING'));

$json = new JsonAccessor('{"name":"x","count":3}');
check('json keeps the string values of an object', $json->all() === ['name' => 'x']);

exit($failures === 0 ? 0 : 1);

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Synthetic\Accessors\Formats;

use Synthetic\Accessors\Accessor;

/** Reads `KEY=value` lines. Blank lines and lines that start with `#` are skipped; a value may be wrapped in one pair of matching quotes. */
final class EnvAccessor implements Accessor
{
    /** @var array<string, string> */
    private array $values = [];

    public function __construct(string $source)
    {
        foreach (preg_split('/\r?\n/', $source) ?: [] as $raw) {
            $line = trim($raw);
            if ($line === '' || str_starts_with($line, '#')) {
                continue;
            }
            $eq = strpos($line, '=');
            if ($eq === false || $eq === 0) {
                continue;
            }
            $key = trim(substr($line, 0, $eq));
            $value = trim(substr($line, $eq + 1));
            if (strlen($value) >= 2 && ($value[0] === '"' || $value[0] === "'") && $value[strlen($value) - 1] === $value[0]) {
                $value = substr($value, 1, -1);
            }
            $this->values[$key] = $value;
        }
    }

    public function get(string $key, ?string $fallback = null): ?string
    {
        return $this->values[$key] ?? $fallback;
    }

    public function has(string $key): bool
    {
        return array_key_exists($key, $this->values);
    }

    public function all(): array
    {
        return $this->values;
    }
}

content.text: Both suites pass. Next I'll record the one call I made that the request didn't spell out: what counts as the `export` prefix.

input.title: EnvAccessor drops a leading `export` followed by spaces or tabs, in both packages
input.rationale: `export KEY=value` is read as `KEY=value`. The prefix is removed from the trimmed line before the comment check and the `=` split, so everything after it behaves exactly as if it had never been written. It is `export` followed by one or more spaces or tabs, so `export   KEY=v` and `export<TAB>KEY=v` work (shell allows both) while `export=1` and `exportKEY=2` keep `export` as a key or part of one. A line with nothing but the prefix, `export KEY` with no `=`, or `export =v` is skipped like its unprefixed form. A `# export X=1` comment stays a comment. The class is spelled `[ \t]` in both packages on purpose: JS `\s` is Unicode-wide and PHP `\s` is ASCII-only, so `\s` would let the two diverge. Made in the JS and the PHP EnvAccessor in the same change, as ADR-1 asks, with the same four test cases in each.
input.alternatives: Strip only the literal string `export ` (one space): rejected, `export  KEY=v` and a tab after export are common in real shell-style files, and the shell accepts them. Use `\s+` for the gap: rejected, it matches different characters in JS (Unicode) and PHP (ASCII), which would break parity on exotic whitespace. Strip `export` from the parsed key afterwards (`key.replace(/^export\s+/)`): rejected, it would let `export =v` and `export` alone slip through differently from the unprefixed form and puts the rule after the `=` split instead of before the line is read. Also accept `declare -x` or `set` forms: rejected, not asked for, and not part of the dotenv habit being covered.

content.text:
`EnvAccessor` now reads `export KEY=value` as `KEY=value`, in both the JS and PHP packages. Both test suites pass (JS 10/10, PHP all `ok`).

I changed both packages because ADR-1 requires a behavior change in one to be made in the other in the same pull request. The `parity-vectors.json` that ADR-1 mentions doesn't exist in this repo, so there were no shared vectors to update.

**How it works**
- The accessor strips a leading `export` plus spaces or tabs after trimming the line and before the comment check and the `=` split. After that the line is parsed as usual, so quoting, comments and blank lines behave as before.
- `export=1` and `exportKEY=2` keep `export` as a key or part of one. `export KEY` (no `=`), `export =value` and `# export X=1` are skipped like their unprefixed forms.
- I wrote the gap as `[ \t]+` rather than `\s+` in both languages. JS `\s` matches Unicode whitespace and PHP `\s` is ASCII-only, so `\s` would let the two diverge on unusual whitespace.

**Tests**
Each package has the same four new cases:
- the basic prefix, including a quoted value
- multiple spaces and a tab
- `export` kept as a key
- the lines that are skipped

**Record**
I recorded this as ADR-2, which is still `proposed`. It covers the whitespace rule and the alternatives I turned down. I didn't supersede or link anything to ADR-1.

**Not committed**
I haven't committed anything, since you didn't ask me to. `git status` shows the four code and test files plus new untracked files under `.mnema/` (a key and a tail). The record should go in the same commit as the code. A hook noted that this session's key founded a new identity in the public tree, mnid:4fdeb6c2. If that identity is you under a new key, the hook's message has the `mnema key request` steps to merge it before you commit.
